lines.text: Be resident in men like one another,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And not in me! I am myself alone.--

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: Clarence, beware! thou keep'st me from the light;

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: But I will sort a pitchy day for thee;

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: For I will buzz abroad such prophecies

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: That Edward shall be fearful of his life,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And then, to purge his fear, I'll be thy death.

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: King Henry and the prince his son are gone;

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: Clarence, thy turn is next, and then the rest,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: Counting myself but bad till I be best.

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: I'll throw thy body in another room,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And triumph, Henry, in thy day of doom.

stage_directions: KING EDWARD is discovered sitting on his throne; QUEEN ELIZABETH with the infant Prince, CLARENCE, Gloster, HASTINGS, and others, near him.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Once more we sit in England's royal throne,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Re-purchas'd with the blood of enemies.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: What valiant foemen, like to autumn's corn,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Have we mow'd down in tops of all their pride!

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Three Dukes of Somerset, threefold renown'd

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: For hardy and undoubted champions;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Two Cliffords, as the father and the son;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And two Northumberlands,--two braver men

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Ne'er spurr'd their coursers at the trumpet's sound;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: With them the two brave bears, Warwick and Montague,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: That in their chains fetter'd the kingly lion

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And made the forest tremble when they roar'd.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Thus have we swept suspicion from our seat

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And made our footstool of security.--

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Come hither, Bess, and let me kiss my boy.--

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Young Ned, for thee thine uncles and myself

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Have in our armours watch'd the winter's night,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Went all afoot in summer's scalding heat,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: That thou mightst repossess the crown in peace;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And of our labours thou shalt reap the gain.

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: I'll blast his harvest if your head were laid;

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: For yet I am not look'd on in the world.

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: This shoulder was ordain'd so thick to heave;

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And heave it shall some weight or break my back.--

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: Work thou the way,--and that shall execute.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Clarence and Gloster, love my lovely queen;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And kiss your princely nephew, brothers both.

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: The duty that I owe unto your Majesty

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: I seal upon the lips of this sweet babe.

lines.speaker: Lady Grey (Queen Elizabeth)
lines.text: Thanks, noble Clarence; worthy brother, thanks.

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And, that I love the tree from whence thou sprang'st,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: Witness the loving kiss I give the fruit.--

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: To say the truth, so Judas kiss'd his Master,

lines.speaker: Richard Plantagenet (Gloucester)
lines.text: And cried, all hail! when as he meant all harm.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Now am I seated as my soul delights;

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Having my country's peace and brothers' loves.

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: What will your Grace have done with Margaret?

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: Reignier, her father, to the King of France

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: Hath pawn'd the Sicils and Jerusalem,

lines.speaker: George, Duke of Clarence
lines.text: And hither have they sent it for her ransom.

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Away with her and waft her hence to France.--

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: And now what rests but that we spend the time

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: With stately triumphs, mirthful comic shows,

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Such as befits the pleasure of the court?

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: Sound drums and trumpets!--farewell sour annoy!

lines.speaker: Edward IV
lines.text: For here, I hope, begins our lasting joy.
